newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - T-bond futures could rise more near term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - T-bond futures could rise more near term.

text.p: September U.S. Treasury bond futures could gain more ground in the near term if the contract manages to continue holding support, chartists said Monday.
After rising early Monday to probe just above the 110-00 resistance area, September T-bonds broke back down on strong economic data but held support at the 100-day moving average at 109-07/32.
The contract then recovered to small gains and hovered near the 200-day moving average at 109-23/32.
"If we can close it up here, above 23-24, it would still look good," one floor chartist said after midday Monday.
"Otherwise, it could be a short-term top," he added. "It could drift lower."
He pegged interim technical support for the contract, which he expected might find additional underpinnings from market talk of a coupon pass this week, at the 109-09/32 area.
"The technicals suggest the long and short ends are still positive," added a Eurodollar floor trader.

He noted that even the pullback Monday morning on the stronger than expected national purchasing managers' index pressured Eurodollars less than he might have expected if the market were ready for an extended downside test.
He noted that December Eurodollars managed to respect support on the decline in the 93.73 to 93.745 area.
Longer term, the performance in the last month by T-bond futures suggests strongly that the long end is ripe for a powerful rise that could take more than a year to complete.

Jim Grauer, president of Omnitrage, had said early Friday that the weekly stochastic for June T-bonds upcrossed April 29. By Friday's close, the daily stochastic had significantly narrowed its negative percent K/D spread to less than one point from a negative eight points.
On Monday, he said that daily upcrossed strongly.
"Today it (daily) actually upcrossed," he said, adding that the daily stochastic rose to a positive 4.5 percent to the upside, reinforcing the weekly.
He also said the monthly is drawing closer to an upcross than it has been since last December, when it suggested but failed to make such a move.
Fundamentals that are currently setting up could portend more gains over the next 15 months in a rise reminiscent of a rally that began in 1994.
"All the elements are in place for a secular rally," he said. "I'm looking at a 120 handle over that 15-month period." ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
